He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Lipscomb Bisons men's basketball|Lipscomb Bisons]] and was named the [[ASUN Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ASUN Conference Player of the Year]] for 2019. ==College career== [[File:Garrison Mathews PIT.jpg|left|150px|thumb|Mathews in 2019]] Mathews was a dual-sport athlete at [[Franklin High School (Tennessee)|Franklin High School]] in [[Franklin, Tennessee]], playing both basketball and [[American football|football]].{{cite web|last=McGaw|first=Sam|title=Lipscomb basketball uses local talent on first trip to Big Dance|url=https://brentwoodhomepage.com/lipscomb-basketball-uses-local-talent-on-first-trip-to-big-dance/|work=brentwoodhomepage.com|access-date=March 9, 2019|date=March 14, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} At [[Lipscomb Bisons men's basketball|Lipscomb]], Mathews dedicated himself solely to basketball for the first time. He became one of the top players in program history, setting the school's [[NCAA Division I|Division I]]-era records in single-game scoring, career scoring, and three-pointers made.{{cite web | title=Mathews scores record 43 points in 86-71 Lipscomb win |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/01/06/mathews-scores-record-43-points-in-86-71-lipscomb-win/109218996/|work=[[USA Today]] |access-date=March 9, 2019|date=January 6, 2018}}{{cite web |last = Organ | first = Mike | title=Garrison Mathews becomes Lipscomb's NCAA Division I all-time leading scorer |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/2019/01/12/lipscomb-garrison-mathews-basketball-all-time-leading-scorer-3-point-shooter/2528227002/|work=[[The Tennessean]] |access-date=March 9, 2019|date=January 12, 2019}} As a junior, Mathews led the Bisons to their first [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As a senior, he was named Atlantic Sun Player of the Year and first-team All-[[ASUN Conference|Atlantic Sun]].{{cite web|last=Organ|first=Mike|date=March 4, 2019|title=Lipscomb's Garrison Mathews named Atlantic Sun Player of the Year, Casey Alexander is Coach of the Year|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/2019/03/04/lipscombs-garrison-mathews-casey-alexander-atlantic-sun-conference-player-year/3057036002/|access-date=March 9, 2019|work=[[The Tennessean]]}}{{cite news|title=Lipscomb's Mathews highlights 2019 @ASUNMBB postseason awards|url=http://asunsports.org/sports/mbkb/2018-19/releases/20190304g27d8n|access-date=March 4, 2019|work=[[ASUN Conference]]|date=March 4, 2019|archive-date=May 8, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190508064210/http://asunsports.org/sports/mbkb/2018-19/releases/20190304g27d8n|url-status=dead}} He also led Lipscomb to a runner-up finish at the [[2019 NIT]]. Mathews scored 44 and 34 points in the tournament's quarterfinals and semifinals, respectively, to help the Bisons reach the championship game, in which they were defeated by [[2018–19 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]]. Mathews averaged 20.8 points per game as a senior and scored 2,478 career points in college. ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards (2019–2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Mathews signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Under the terms of the deal he divided his time between the Wizards and the [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite news|first=Mike|last=Organ|title=Lipscomb's Garrison Mathews signs two-way deal with Washington Wizards|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/2019/06/21/nba-draft-lipscomb-garrison-mathews-signs-two-way-deal-washington-wizards/1520337001/|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=June 21, 2019|access-date=June 21, 2019}} On October 23, 2019, Mathews made his NBA debut, coming off the bench in a 100–108 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] with an assist, playing only one minute.{{cite web|title=Doncic-Porzingis debut carries Mavs past Wizards, 108-100|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160631|website=ESPN.com|date=October 23, 2019|access-date=October 23, 2019}} On December 30, Mathews scored a career-high 28 points with four rebounds in a 123–105 win over the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|title=McRae, Mathews lead depleted Wizards past Heat 123-105|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161134|website=ESPN.com|date=December 30, 2019|access-date=December 31, 2019}} ===Houston Rockets (2021–2023)=== On September 28, 2021, Mathews signed with the [[Boston Celtics]],{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/boston-celtics-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=September 28, 2021|access-date=October 3, 2021}} but was waived at the end of training camp.{{cite tweet|author=Keith Smith|number=1449501516344266752|title=Official Boston Celtics waivers: Chris Clemons Luke Kornet Garrison Mathews Theo Pinson Boston now has 16 players under contract. 15 standard deals, 1 Two-Way deal. One Two-Way spot remains open for the Celtics.|user=KeithSmithNBA|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On October 18, he was claimed off waivers by the [[Houston Rockets]], who later turned his deal into a two-way contract with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite web|title= Rockets Claim Garrison Mathews off Waivers|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-claim-garrison-mathews-waivers|first=Trevor|last=Patin|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2021|access-date=October 18, 2021}} On December 18, the Rockets announced they had converted Mathews' two-way deal to a four-year, $8.2 million standard contract.{{cite web|title=Rockets Announce Roster Changes|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-announce-roster-changes|first=Hiren|last=Joshi|website=NBA.com|date=December 18, 2021|access-date=December 18, 2021}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2023–2025)=== On February 9, 2023, Mathews and [[Bruno Fernando]] were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Justin Holiday]], [[Frank Kaminsky]] and two future second-round draft picks.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-four-player-trade-with-atlanta|title=Rockets Complete Four-Player Trade with Atlanta |first=Hiren|last=Joshi|work=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023}} He made nine appearances for the team over the remainder of the year, posting averages of 4.8 points, 1.4 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Garrison Mathews 2022-23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3913180/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=December 26, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} Mathews made 66 appearances (five starts) for Atlanta during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 4.9 points, 1.4 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Garrison Mathews 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3913180/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=December 26, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} He played in 47 games (including two starts) for the Hawks in the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 7.5 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 1.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Garrison Mathews 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3913180/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=December 26, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} On September 16, 2025, Mathews signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[New York Knicks]].{{Cite web |title=New York Knicks Sign Garrison Matthews To An Exhibit 10 Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-sign-garrison-mathews-to-an-exhibit-10-contract |access-date=October 24, 2025 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} He was waived by the Knicks prior to the start of the regular season on October 18.{{cite web | title=Knicks officially release Alex Len, Garrison Mathews and Matt Ryan | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=2025-10-18 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/knicks-officially-release-alex-len-210559564.html | access-date=2025-12-06}} ===Indiana Pacers (2025)=== Mathews signed a 10-day contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]] on November 20, 2025, after the team was granted a hardship exception.[https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-granted-hardship-exception-251120 "Indiana Pacers Granted Hardship Exception"] ''NBA.com''. November 20, 2025. Retrieved November 21, 2025. On December 1, the Pacers re-signed Mathews to a second 10-day hardship contract.East, Tony (December 1, 2025). [https://www.forbes.com/sites/tonyeast/2025/12/01/pacers-to-bring-back-garrison-mathews-on-second-10-day-hardship-deal/ "Pacers To Bring Back Garrison Mathews On Second 10-Day Hardship Deal"]. ''Forbes''. Retrieved December 1, 2025. On December 11, Mathews signed a non-guaranteed standard contract with the team for the remainder of the season.Dopirak, Dustin (December 12, 2025). [https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2025/12/12/garrison-mathews-pacers-3-point-shooting-jeremiah-robinson-earl/87721833007/ "Why the Pacers kept Garrison Mathews: 'Guys like that change the game'"] ''[[The Indianapolis Star]]''. Retrieved December 12, 2025. In 15 appearances (one start) for the Pacers, he averaged 5.2 points, 1.1 rebounds, and 0.7 assists. On December 26, Mathews was waived by Indiana following the signing of [[Micah Potter]].{{Cite web|title=Indiana Pacers To Sign Center Micah Potter, Waive Garrison Matthews|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tonyeast/2025/12/26/indiana-pacers-to-sign-center-micah-potter-waive-garrison-mathews/|access-date=December 26, 2025|website=forbes.com|language=en}} sharpshooting guard Garrison Mathews|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/milan-swoops-for-guard-garrison-mathews/|date=August 18,
